items.title: Max Miller Continues to Resist Pressure to Drop Out as Deadline Looms
items.author: Emily Davies and Annie Karni
items.content: <article>The Republican House member from Ohio was accused of holding a gun to his ex-wife’s head and fracturing the collarbone of their young daughter. He has denied the accusations.</article>

items.title: Former Marine Is Unresponsive After Mistreatment in Russian Detention, Family Says
items.author: Isabella Kwai
items.content: <article>Robert Gilman, 32, was being fed through a tube and in a “dissociative stupor,” an advocacy group said. He was arrested in Russia in 2022.</article>

items.title: Blanche Is Confirmed as Attorney General After Overcoming G.O.P. Concerns
items.author: Michael Gold, Glenn Thrush and Carl Hulse
items.content: <article>Todd Blanche, who has served as acting attorney general since April, eked out Senate approval, despite growing unease about his willingness to rein in President Trump.</article>

items.title: Trump Officials Under Pressure to Deport Haitians After Supreme Court Win on T.P.S. Program
items.author: Madeleine Ngo and Hamed Aleaziz
items.content: <article>The lack of visible raids aggressively targeting Haitians who lost temporary status has frustrated some of President Trump’s most fervent supporters.</article>

items.title: A Spurned Schumer Reaches Out to the Left
items.author: Carl Hulse
items.content: <article>In a phone call this week, the Democratic leader told the new Michigan Senate nominee who had opposed him to just win, working to foster unity ahead of a difficult race.</article>

items.title: U.S. Squeezes Cuba Even as It Searches for a New Regime Leader
items.author: Tyler Pager, Julian E. Barnes and Frances Robles
items.content: <article>Some officials warn that a more hard-line leader could emerge if the Trump administration moves forward with its plans.</article>

items.title: They’re Battle-Tested Democrats. Do Voters Care?
items.author: Jess Bidgood
items.content: <article>Haley Stevens and Angie Craig were celebrated by Democrats in 2018. This year, they’ve faced tough primaries.</article>

items.title: Charles S. Faddis, Ex-C.I.A. Officer Who Pushed Conspiracy Theories, Dies at 68
items.author: Trip Gabriel
items.content: <article>After 20 years in the C.I.A., he emerged as an outspoken critic of the agency and as a leader of the election-denial movement in Pennsylvania.</article>

items.title: Senate Passes Sanctions Bill Targeting Russia and Iran
items.author: Robert Jimison
items.content: <article>The legislation was championed by Senator Lindsey Graham, the South Carolina Republican whose sudden death last month helped spur quick action on it.</article>

items.title: Appeals Court Upholds Block on Trump Ballroom Construction
items.author: Zach Montague and Mattathias Schwartz
items.content: <article>A federal appeals court panel backed a lower court’s ruling, and made it likely that the Supreme Court will decide the case. But the decision does not mean construction will halt immediately.</article>

items.title: Iranians Say Trump’s Promises Have Fallen by the Wayside as Iran War Drags On
items.author: Erica L. Green, Zolan Kanno-Youngs, Sanam Mahoozi and Yeganeh Torbati
items.content: <article>As President Trump struggles to extricate the United States from the war in Iran, his promises to protesters in the country have fallen by the wayside.</article>

items.title: Don Lemon Accuses Justice Dept. of Vindictive Prosecution in Church Protest Case
items.author: Alan Feuer
items.content: <article>Lawyers for the former CNN anchor asked a judge to throw out the case, saying prosecutors had “acted on the president’s animus by filing unprecedented charges against a journalist for doing his job.”</article>

items.title: Prosecutor Sues Justice Dept. Over Dismissal After Right-Wing Influencer’s Claim
items.author: Alan Feuer
items.content: <article>Will Rosenzweig joins a growing list of former prosecutors and federal agents who have gone to court to contest the purge of law enforcement deemed disloyal.</article>
